intro: A tangent to a circle is a line that touches the circle at exactly one point. At the point of contact, the tangent is perpendicular to the radius. From a point outside a circle we can draw exactly two tangents, and they are equal in length.
keyPoints: There is exactly one tangent at any point on a circle.
Tangent ⟂ radius at the point of contact.
No tangent can be drawn from a point inside the circle; two tangents can be drawn from a point outside.
Lengths of the two tangents from an external point are equal.
If the angle between two tangents is θ, the angle they subtend at the centre is 180° − θ.
formulas: Tangent length from P: PT = √(OP² − r²)
